newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rejects labour, rights issues at WTO.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rejects labour, rights issues at WTO.

text.p: Indonesia will oppose any declaration by the World Trade Organisation (WTO) that includes human rights and labour standards, the Jakarta Post daily said on Wednesday.

"Indonesia will reject the inclusion of social issues, such as human rights and labour standards because the discussion of such issues is not the responsibility of the WTO, but of the ILO (International Labour Organisation)," the newspaper quoted Industry and Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo as saying.
Tunky will head the Indonesian delegation at WTO's inaugural ministerial meeting in Singapore next week.

Tunky said Indonesia would also reject a proposed multilateral investment policy because the proposal by some developed countries concerned matters which violated state sovereignty. "We do need foreign investment. However, we should have the right to regulate it," Tunky said.

Several developed countries including the United States and Japan proposed a multilateral investment treaty to make WTO member countries treat foreign and domestic investors equally, the newspaper said.
Indonesia would also reject any inclusion regarding government procurement policies because state purchases were the prerogative of any sovereign state, Tungky said.
However, Indonesia would agree in principle to a U.S. proposal to liberalise trade in computers and related information technology products by 2000, the paper said.
Tungky said Indonesia would express its concerns over the slow integration of the multi-fibre arrangement, which governs international trade on textiles and garments, into the WTO.
As a textile exporting country, Indonesia wanted a speedy integration of the arrangement into the WTO and wanted textile importing countries to abolish their quota system, he said.
